newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico offers full support to deaf-mute "slaves".
newsitem.headline: Mexico offers full support to deaf-mute "slaves".

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Wednesday vowed to do everything to help his deaf-mute compatriots who suffered virtual slavery in New York, and vowed to punish the perpetrators of what he called such "atrocities."
Mexicans were shocked by news this week that dozens of their deaf-mute compatriots had been held captive and forced to peddle trinkets for a pittance on the streets of New York City.

In a speech in Chicago late on Wednesday, the visiting Mexican president called the discoveries "atrocities" and pledged to punish anyone caught sumggling immigrants into the United States from Mexico.

"The adequate response consists of the severest punishment under the terms of the law for those who traffic in disabled people, and of complete support to unite (this group) with their families and their communities," Zedillo said.
"My government will firmly honour this response," he said.
In a statement received from the Interior Ministry late on Wednesday, Mexico also promised the victims full consular protection and legal advice.
Once their migration status has been clarified, Mexico said that in case they were repatriated it would help them reach their place or origin or another of their choosing.
It also promised to help them make contact with family or friends in Mexico.

U.S. officials rescued 57 people, 12 of them children, from two cramped New York City apartments over the weekend after four deaf-mute Mexicans walked into a New York City police station and told their bizarre tale.

Speaking via sign-language interpreters, they said they had been smuggled from Mexico into southern California and transported to Los Angeles and New York City where they were forced to work for slave wages and suffered serious abuse.
On Monday police arrested seven people and arraigned four of them in a federal court in New York City.
They were charged in a conspiracy to bring, transport and conceal illegal aliens. If convicted, each faces a possible prison sentence of 10 years for each illegal alien involved.
But U.S. and Mexican police said they were still searching for a Mexican man believed to be the ringleader and whom they identified as Reinaldo Paoletti.
Mexico said it would do everything to help find all those responsible.
"The National Migration Institute will collaborate in the corresponding investigations to identify the individuals who could be involved in the trafficking of people into the United States," it said.
The Mexicans are in the custody of city authorities and the American Red Cross is providing them with housing and food until their immigration status is determined.
